To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
subthreshold membrane potential modulates neurotransmitter release by affecting action potential shape, and that the Kv1 family potassium channels Kv1.1 and Kv1.2 are necessary for this modulation.
subthreshold modulation of action potential shape is abolished by a Kv1.1 channel mutation, but not by Kv1.1 knockout, and that Kv1.1 is not required for modulation.

In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental question: How does information encoded as a graded membrane potential at the soma of a nerve cell become converted to the all-or-none action potential?
the mechanisms underlying analog-to-digital conversion in neurons.
the modulation of presynaptic spike shape and its effect on neurotransmitter release, which depends on the interplay of two mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Kv1.1 channelopathies affect the composition and voltage dependence of presynaptic voltage-gated potassium channels, which in turn determine the basal spike width as well as the modulation of spike width by subthreshold somatically generated depolarization.

the Kv1 subfamily of potassium channels is necessary for the modulation of action potential shape by somatic subthreshold depolarization, but that this modulation is not mediated by the Kv1. 1 channel itself.

the Kv1 subfamily of K+ channels plays a key role in shaping the presynaptic action potential waveform and in the modulation of the waveform by somatic depolarizing prepulses, and that the Kv1 channels are not necessary for the modulation, but rather that a disease-associated mutant prevents the modulation by interfering with the stoichiometry of the channel complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Kv1.1 is not required for subthreshold spike broadening, but a mutation in Kv1.1 abolishes this modulation.
Kv1.1 channelopathies prevent the interplay of subthreshold and all-or-none transmission at the presynaptic terminal.
Kv1.1 channelopathies abolish analog–digital modulation of presynaptic spikes by subthreshold somatodendritic depolarization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
subthreshold membrane potential modulates neurotransmission by affecting spike shape.
the Kv1 family of potassium channels is essential for analog-digital modulation in hippocampal axons.
subthreshold somatic fluctuations can modulate the release of neurotransmitter.
